patch_description:
The original program failed validation because its recursive path returned an empty `column_orderings` list (`return final_result_df, []`), gave no valid per-row column permutations, mutated/rebuilt DataFrames with mismatched column names (e.g. renaming the last column to "original_index"), relied on `itertuples` attribute lookups that break with non-identifier/duplicate column names, and printed debug output. The whole approach also optimized the wrong objective (squared field lengths / adjacent grouping) instead of character-level Trie prefix reuse.

The fix replaces the editable block with a self-contained, correct implementation that preserves all data and shape:
- Serializes each cell once (missing → "", otherwise `str(v)`) and reuses these strings across all candidate constructions.
- Builds up to three cheap candidate per-row column orderings: (1) a global frequency ordering ranked by Σ len(v)·count·(count−1), (2) a bounded conditional partition tree (choose a leading field by length-weighted pair repetition, partition rows by its value, order suffixes separately per group, bounded depth/group size/candidate columns), and (3) an alternative frequency/length tradeoff ordering.
- Scores each candidate with the exact ideal serial-Trie objective (sum of adjacent LCPs of the sorted serialized rows, computed with C-speed binary-search prefix-slice comparisons), and returns the best.
- Honors `col_merge` (merged columns kept adjacent) and `one_way_dep` (dependent column placed right after its dependency) as ordering constraints, uses `col_stop`/`row_stop` as recursion-depth bounds and `distinct_value_threshold` to bar overly-distinct columns from being partition fields, and returns valid per-row column orderings consistent with the returned DataFrame (whose columns are placed in the modal row ordering as a hedge). No data values are altered, added, dropped, or fabricated.
